author: Roseann Cattani
title: Salinas puts a pause on issuing new tobacco retail licenses - NewsBreak
text:
By Roseann Cattani ,
5 hours ago
The city of Salinas will temporarily pause issuing new tobacco retail licenses to review regulations and help prevent youth access to tobacco products, the Salinas City Council approved on Tuesday, June 30.
As of March, there are 124 active tobacco retailers in Salinas, most located in grocery stores, liquor stores, gas stations and convenience stores. In recent years, however, the city has seen an increase in standalone “smoke shop” tobacco retailers.
Currently, Salinas does not have restrictions on how close tobacco retailers can operate to youth-centered areas such as schools, parks , recreation centers and childcare facilities. Many municipalities across the state have adopted restrictions, according to the staff report, such as limiting the number of retail licenses issued based on population (per capita) and/or location considerations.
City staff said in a presentation to the council that the 45-day moratorium, which can be extended by the city council, will allow time to evaluate these concerns, including potential conflicts related to permitted uses under existing tobacco retail licenses.
City staff said they will also be reviewing the city's cannabis retail laws.
Say hello to 'Sali' the city’s new virtual assistant The AI revolution has arrived at city hall.
The city of Salinas announced the launch of "Sali" a new virtual assistant (or chat bot) on the city website, which people can use to find information about city services or learn about city projects and initiatives.
Instead of scrolling through the city’s website at www.salinas.gov people can ask "Sali" a question and she will send you a list of options. People can find out how to apply for a city permit, open a service request through SalinasCONNECT, register a rental property or find landlord or other housing resources.
"Sali" is available 24 hours a day and she speaks Spanish. You can also shoot her a text message at 877-357-SALI.
This article originally appeared on Salinas Californian: Salinas puts a pause on issuing new tobacco retail licenses
